question: The simple interest on a sum of money is (9)/(45) of the sum. If the number of years is numerically 5 times of rate per cent per annum, then find the rate per cent per annum.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective Rate % over the entire period = (SI ÷ P) × 100

Rate × Time = (9 ÷ 45) × 100

Given Time (T) = 5R, we substitute T directly:

R × 5R = (1 ÷ 5) × 100

5R² = 20 ⇒ R² = 4 ⇒ R = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Simple Interest (SI) = 9/45 of Principal (P) = P / 5

Time (T) = 5 × Rate (R)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5a232f74cbdfb1e03ef873f586e46e9e4409857ace4658cb8bb6a17f60e8a998.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ P / 5 = (P × R × 5R) ÷ 100

Dividing both sides by P:

⇒ 1 / 5 = 5R² / 100

⇒ 1 / 5 = R² / 20

⇒ R² = 20 / 5

⇒ R² = 4

⇒ R = √4 = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest (SI) Basics

Simple interest is charged only on the initial principal for the entire duration. The formula is SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Important Variation Formulas

Principal (P) = (SI × 100) ÷ (R × T) | Time (T) = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × R)

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

SI grows linearly over time, whereas Compound Interest (CI) grows exponentially because interest is calculated on both the principal and the accumulated interest.
